content.text: Atherosclerotic dz of the arteries of the lower extremities
*Leriche’s Syndrome: triad of buttock/thigh claud + impotence + ↓ femoral pulses
: in advanced dz; MC @ night & relieved w/ foot dependency
– musc atrophy, thin/shiny skin, hair loss, thickened nails cool limbs, areas of necrosis; USU ⍉edema
•>1.2 → poss noncompressible (calcified) vessels – may lead to a false reading
– USU only performed if revasc = planned
smoke cessation assoc w/ greatest benefit
most effective medical therapy; ASA, clopidogrel, pentoxifylline
: percut transluminal angioplasty (first line revasc procedure) bypass grafts, endarterectomy (last line)
– rapidly developing or sudden decrease in limb perf
MC in the superfic femoral or popliteal a.
late finding assoc w/ a worse prognosis
); sxs USU dist to the occlusion
An STAT threatened limb may undergo further eval & tx in a surg suite
, endarterectomy; thrombolytic therapy or percut angioplasty
Supportive: pain control, fluid resuscitation, UFH
